nodes.label: Essay Approach Session (Phase 1)
nodes.rationale: Locks task, plan+thesis, in-distribution corpus, background reading corpus, rubric, citation conventions, and AI-detection threshold (default 15%, pushed to 5% under strict AI policy) before any drafting; the background corpus is also passed to the rubric and citation reviewers.

nodes.label: Essay Four-Reviewer Iteration Loop (Phase 2)
nodes.rationale: Reviewers run in parallel each round; the next draft addresses the weakest axis first. Exit on all thresholds passing or after 5 rounds without convergence. State is saved every round so the loop is resumable after a crash. Never pad a draft to satisfy a metric: a 2:1 with integrity beats a Distinction with hallucinated citations.

nodes.label: Synthetic Reference Corpus Ban
nodes.rationale: If no real references or quasi-exemplar exist, the in-distribution reviewer is dropped entirely rather than pivoting to synthetic essays: a sub-agent's in-distribution judgement against essays generated by another sub-agent is a fake signal, uninformative about a real human marker. The loop then runs on 3 reviewers.

nodes.label: Pre-Review Anonymisation (citation-date stripping)
nodes.rationale: All citation dates are replaced with YEAR placeholders across the user's draft AND every reference essay so the adversarial critic cannot cheat by picking the essay with the newest sources as the odd one out, which is a non-signal, not a quality differentiator. Names, candidate numbers, URLs/DOIs revealing dates, and PDF metadata are also stripped.

nodes.label: AI Detection Reviewer (gptzero.py module)
nodes.rationale: A Python module, not a sub-agent: gptzero.py (reverse-engineered AI detector) returns per-sentence and overall AI-likelihood JSON. Threshold pass is overall likelihood below the Phase 1 target.
